items.passage: We enter the principal room, at one end of which is a big bed, while nearer the door is a table with wine and glasses, and fruit, and specimens of lava and other matters. My friend, with the recklessness of youth, spends his money. I refuse to do anything of the kind; and again our coachman urges on his wild career. He pulls up again as a woman rushes out of her cabin to offer us drink. Again we are tempted, and in vain. Then we reach a level of reeds and rushes, where resides a venerable and unwashed hermit, who sighs as he turns in and thinks of the hardness of our hearts.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from cheerful anticipation to bitter regret over money spent.
It moves from anxious fear of the coachman to calm relief at arrival.
It moves from plain description of a room to playful mock-solemnity.
It moves from admiring praise of the hermit to open scorn for him.
items.explanation: 지문은 방 안의 사물을 담담히 묘사하다가, 여관·여인·은자의 유혹을 거듭 물리치는 과정을 과장된 엄숙함으로 서술한다. 특히 은자가 '우리 마음의 완고함'을 한탄한다는 대목은 장난스러운 모의 진지함을 드러내므로 C가 정답이다. A의 후회, B의 두려움, D의 경멸은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Despite this hint, the lesson is enforced upon the children, but there is no evidence that it bears fruit in their homes to any noticeable extent, as is the case with the Italians I spoke of. The homes are too hopeless, the grind too unceasing. The managers know it and have little hope of the older immigrants. It is toward getting hold of their children that they bend every effort, and with a success that shows how easily these children can be moulded for good or for bad. Nor do they let go their grasp of them until the job is finished.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from praise of the Italians to criticism of the managers.
It moves from confidence in the lesson to doubt about the children.
It moves from sympathy for older immigrants to anger at the children.
It moves from discouragement about the homes to resolve about the children.
items.explanation: 앞부분은 가정이 '너무 절망적'이고 노인 이민자에게 희망이 적다는 낙담의 어조이다. 이후 '아이들을 붙잡는 데 모든 노력을 기울인다'며 결의와 성공의 어조로 바뀌므로 D가 정답이다. A는 이탈리아인이 비교 대상일 뿐이고, B와 C는 아이들에 대한 지문의 긍정적 평가와 반대된다.

items.passage: Sensible women may always have a good measure of political influence of the right sort, if they choose. And it is in one sense a duty on their part to claim this influence, and to exert it, but always in the true womanly way. The influence of good sense, of a sound judgment, of good feeling may always he theirs. Let us see that we preserve this influence, and that we use it wisely. But let us cherish our happy immunities as women by keeping aloof from all public personal action in the political field.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from urging women to use influence to cautioning against public action.
It moves from mocking women's political views to praising their quiet sense.
It moves from doubting women's judgment to demanding full political rights.
It moves from calmly describing a duty to angrily rejecting all influence.
items.explanation: 화자는 먼저 여성이 분별력과 판단력으로 정치적 영향력을 행사하는 것이 의무라고 권한다. 그러나 'But'으로 시작하는 마지막 문장에서 공적 정치 활동은 멀리하라고 경고하는 어조로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B의 조롱, C의 권리 요구, D의 분노는 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: On Twelfth Night the little ones were christened, and then the trooper bethought himself of his promise to get back soon. The storms had ceased, but worse had befallen; the sea was frozen over as far as eye reached, and the island was cut off from all communication with the outer world. There was nothing for it but to wait. It proved the longest and hardest winter any one then living could remember. Easter was at hand before the ice broke up, and let a fishing smack slip over to Ystad, on the mainland. It came back with news that set the whole island wondering.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It recounts a christening in detail, then explains why the trooper never returned.
It describes a delay caused by the frozen sea, then hints at surprising news.
It praises the island's winter beauty, then contrasts it with the mainland.
It presents the trooper's promise, then shows him breaking it on purpose.
items.explanation: 지문은 기병이 곧 돌아가겠다던 약속을 떠올렸지만 바다가 얼어 섬이 고립되었다고 전한다. 이어 유난히 길었던 겨울과 부활절 무렵 해빙을 거쳐, 섬 전체를 놀라게 한 소식이 왔다는 암시로 끝나므로 B가 정답이다. A는 세례식을 자세히 묘사하지 않고, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
Ay, but to the riveting of that chain there went an oath, from which the mere fact of his having grown tired of wearing its fetters does not, in his opinion, release him. He is bound by an engagement the more perversely sacred, because none can hold him to it.

Only by her with whom it was made can he be emancipated from it; and for that emancipation how can he ask her? How can he go to her and say, 'I have grown tired of you; I have grown fond of another woman. Let me go!'

It is only as a free gift from her hand that he can accept his dismissal; and, of the improbability of her ever making him that gift, his sinking spirit assures him.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes how he came to love another woman, then recounts their meeting.
It argues that oaths are meaningless, then illustrates this with his departure.
It presents his binding oath, explains who alone can release him, then doubts she will.
It imagines the woman's reply, then shows her willingly granting his freedom.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 그가 지겨워졌어도 맹세에 묶여 있다고 말한다. 다음으로 그 맹세를 한 상대만이 그를 풀어 줄 수 있다고 설명하고, 마지막에 그녀가 그런 선물을 줄 가능성이 낮다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 C가 정답이며, A·B·D는 지문에 없는 만남·주장·허락을 담고 있다.

items.passage: The testimony in such a case must, under the conditions of the present life, be forever inaccessible. It lies wholly outside the range of experience. However abundant it may be, we cannot expect to meet with it. And accordingly our failure to produce it does not raise even the slightest presumption against our theory. When conceived in this way, the belief in a future life is without scientific support; but at the same time it is placed beyond the need of scientific support and beyond the range of scientific criticism.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents evidence for a future life, then dismisses opposing objections.
It criticizes belief in a future life, then urges readers to abandon it.
It recounts a personal experience, then generalizes it into a theory.
It claims the evidence is unreachable, then draws a conclusion about criticism.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 그런 증언이 경험의 범위 밖에 있어 접근할 수 없다고 말한다. 그로부터 증거를 내놓지 못해도 이론에 불리하지 않다고 추론하고, 결국 그 믿음이 과학적 비판의 범위 밖에 있다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, A는 증거 제시, B는 믿음 포기 촉구, C는 개인 경험으로 잘못 설명한다.

items.passage:
On the other hand they suffered from the cold to a degree that was also unaccountable to me. On many occasions I have heard my camel-driver moan from pain in his frozen toes and fingers, but, true enough, when out in the open desert the wind was rather penetrating, and his clothes, barring a waistcoat, consisted of thin white cotton garments. Personally, I never had occasion to make a change in my tropical clothing (I could not if I had wanted to), nor did I ever once have to use an overcoat. But--I seldom know what it is to feel cold.

We delayed our departure the next morning to see if the gale would abate, but at 10 a.m. we had to venture out.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It contrasts the driver's suffering from cold with the narrator's ease, then turns to the next day.
It describes the desert's extreme heat, then recounts the narrator's sudden illness.
It complains about the narrator's own clothing, then praises the driver's endurance.
It gives a history of camel travel, then describes a violent storm in detail.
items.explanation: 지문은 낙타몰이꾼이 얼어붙은 손발 때문에 신음했다고 전한 뒤, 화자 자신은 열대 옷만으로도 추위를 거의 느끼지 않았다고 대조한다. 그리고 새 단락에서 다음 날 아침 출발 이야기로 넘어가므로 A가 정답이다. B의 더위와 병, C의 불평, D의 역사 서술은 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
Of all things in this world to make the heart sick, there is nothing like facing a moral crisis, which some one you love is about to go through, without any feeling of certainty that he will meet it in the one only right way. “Oh, if it was only me!” Elsie sighed, from the bottom of her heart.

__You will think it was the deepest presumption on her part, to think she could meet the emergency better than her father would.__ And so it was, and yet not so at all. It was only that there were no doubts in her mind, and there were doubts, she knew, inconceivable doubts, shadows, self-deceptions, on his.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals that Elsie's father has already failed to meet the crisis.
It anticipates a reader's judgment of Elsie that the narrator then qualifies.
It shows Elsie openly criticizing her father's handling of the matter.
It introduces a new character who doubts Elsie's ability to help.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 독자가 엘시를 주제넘다고 여길 것이라고 미리 말한다. 바로 뒤에서 서술자는 '그렇기도 하고 전혀 그렇지 않기도 하다'며 그녀에게는 의심이 없을 뿐이라고 단서를 단다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, 아버지의 실패(A), 공개 비판(C), 새 인물(D)은 지문에 없다.

items.passage: The words she had said to Fly were quite true. She had looked at herself. Sometimes that sight is very terrible. Her fingers trembled, her whole body shook, but she did not take a moment to make up her mind. They all hated her, but not more than she hated herself. They were quite right to hate her, quite right to feel horror at her presence. __Her mother had often spoken to her of the consequences of unbridled passion, but no words that her mother could ever have used came up to the grim reality.__ Of course, she must go away, and at once. She sat down on the side of her bed, pressed her hand to her forehead, and reflected.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a flashback explaining why the others have come to hate her.
It shows that she blames her mother for failing to warn her properly.
It stresses how terrible her self-knowledge is by contrasting it with past warnings.
It reveals that she has decided to stay and ask the others for forgiveness.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 어머니가 자주 경고했던 말도 지금 마주한 '냉혹한 현실'에는 미치지 못했다고 말한다. 이는 앞에서 자기 모습을 본 것이 '끔찍하다'고 한 깨달음의 무게를 강조하므로 C가 정답이다. A의 회상 설명, B의 어머니 탓, D의 머무르기 결정은 지문과 맞지 않으며 그녀는 오히려 떠나기로 한다.

items.passage:
I answer, that nothing is easier--nothing is more common--nothing more natural to simple-minded people. Never creature had more title than I to speak confidently of this, from experience which melts my heart day by day. “Speaking the truth in love,” is the way. One who does this cannot but be an angel of consolation. __Everything but truth becomes loathed in a sick-room.__ The restless can repose on nothing but this: the sharpened intellectual appetite can be satisfied with nothing less substantial; the susceptible spiritual taste can be gratified with nothing less genuine, noble, and fair.

Then the question arises, what sort of truth?
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a question that the narrator later admits cannot be answered.
It shifts the focus from truthful speech to the details of a physical illness.
It contradicts the narrator's earlier claim that speaking truth is easy.
It offers a general observation that supports the narrator's praise of truth.
items.explanation: 화자는 '사랑 안에서 진실을 말하는 것'이 길이라고 주장한다. 밑줄 문장은 병실에서는 진실 외의 모든 것이 싫어진다는 일반적 관찰로, 이어지는 문장들과 함께 그 주장을 뒷받침하므로 D가 정답이다. A의 질문은 나중에 나오지만 답할 수 없다고 하지 않고, B와 C는 지문의 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: I then thought, as I still think, that the men themselves were actuated by proper motives, and often by very high motives, in joining the regiments. __No doubt they looked to the pay offered.__ It is not often that men are able to devote themselves to patriotism without any reference to their personal circumstances. A man has got before him the necessity of earning his bread, and very frequently the necessity of earning the bread of others besides himself. This comes before him not only as his first duty, but as the very law of his existence.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It concedes a practical motive while preserving the claim that the men meant well.
It rejects the narrator's earlier view that the men had proper motives.
It introduces the narrator's own reasons for joining the regiments.
It criticizes the regiments for offering the men too little pay.
items.explanation: 화자는 먼저 병사들이 올바르고 숭고한 동기로 입대했다고 말한다. 밑줄 문장은 그들이 급여도 고려했다고 인정하되, 뒤 문장들에서 생계가 첫째 의무라고 설명해 앞의 주장을 유지하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 주장을 뒤집는다고 잘못 보고, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
Where the ball passed, not one of us precisely knew; but I fancy it must have been over our heads, and that the wind of it may have contributed to our disaster.

At any rate, the boat sank by the stern, quite gently, in three feet of water, leaving the captain and myself, facing each other, on our feet. The other three took complete headers, and came up again, drenched and bubbling.

So far there was no great harm. No lives were lost, and we could wade ashore in safety. But there were all our stores at the bottom, and, to make things worse, only two guns out of five remained in a state for service. Mine I had snatched from my knees and held over my head, by a sort of instinct.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: He regards the sinking with calm good humor while noting the real losses.
He recalls the sinking with lasting terror and shame at his own panic.
He blames the captain angrily for steering the boat into danger.
He shows complete indifference to the loss of the stores and guns.
items.explanation: 화자는 배가 '아주 부드럽게' 석 자 물에 가라앉아 선장과 마주 선 채 남았다고 담담하고 익살스럽게 묘사한다. 동시에 식량이 가라앉고 총 다섯 정 중 두 정만 남았다는 실제 손실도 짚으므로 A가 정답이다. B의 공포, C의 비난은 근거가 없고, D는 '설상가상'이라는 표현과 모순된다.

items.passage:
I was not very uncomfortable, for I had not been all over into the water. I drove down to the lumber shed, took the squire in, and headed towards home. The senator was shivering with cold, though fortunately it was a very warm day for the season, and he did not absolutely suffer.

It had been cloudy and threatening rain all the afternoon and evening, and before we reached the main road it began to pour in torrents. I had an oil-cloth, which I put over the trunk and the mail. Under ordinary circumstances, a seven-mile ride in such a heavy rain would have been a great misfortune; but, as both of us had been in the river, it did not make much difference to us.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: He feels bitter frustration that the rain ruined an otherwise pleasant trip.
He accepts the downpour practically, since they were already soaked.
He is consumed by worry that the senator will fall seriously ill.
He takes quiet amusement in the squire's unfortunate soaking.
items.explanation: 화자는 평소라면 7마일을 폭우 속에 가는 것이 큰 불운이었겠지만, 둘 다 이미 강에 빠졌으니 별 차이가 없다고 말한다. 또 자신은 그리 불편하지 않았고 상원의원도 따뜻한 날씨 덕에 크게 고생하지 않았다고 하므로 B가 정답이다. A의 원망, C의 깊은 걱정, D의 조롱은 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
"See, Winter comes, to rule the varied year,
Sullen and sad, with all his rising train,
Vapours, and clouds, and storms. Be these my theme,
These! that exalt the soul to solemn thought,
And heavenly musing. Welcome, kindred glooms!
Congenial horrors, hail! with frequent foot,
Pleased have I, in my cheerful morn of life,
When nursed by careless Solitude I lived,
And sung of Nature with unceasing joy,
Pleased have I wander'd through your rough domain;
Trod the pure virgin-snows, myself as pure;
Heard the winds roar, and the big torrents burst;
Or seen the deep-fermenting tempest brew'd
In the grim evening sky. Thus passed the time,
Till through the lucid chambers of the south
Look'd out the joyous Spring, look'd out, and smiled!"
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: He dreads winter's arrival and longs only for the return of spring.
He treats winter with indifference, since it no longer affects him.
He welcomes winter's storms as kindred companions that lift the soul.
He regrets ever having wandered through winter's harsh domain.
items.explanation: 화자는 겨울의 증기·구름·폭풍이 영혼을 '엄숙한 사색'으로 고양시킨다며 노래의 주제로 삼는다. 이어 '반가운 동족 같은 어둠'이라 부르며 젊은 시절 기쁘게 그 거친 영역을 거닐었다고 회상하므로 C가 정답이다. A의 두려움, B의 무관심, D의 후회는 '기뻤다'는 반복 표현과 모순된다.

items.passage: I have achieved none of those objects which the instinct of mankind especially prompts them to pursue, and the accomplishment of which must therefore beget a native satisfaction. The truly wise, after all their speculations, will be led into the common path, and, in homage to the human nature that pervades them, will gather gold, and till the earth, and set out trees, and build a house. But I have scorned such wisdom. I have rejected, also, the settled, sober, careful gladness of a man by his own fireside, with those around him whose welfare is committed to his trust and all their guidance to his fond authority.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: He takes triumphant pride in having escaped the common path of others.
He resents the wise for gathering gold while he remained poor.
He is confused about which goals mankind instinctively pursues.
He admits with rueful candor that he has spurned what others value.
items.explanation: 화자는 인간이 본능적으로 추구하는 목표를 하나도 이루지 못했다고 고백한다. 이어 현명한 이들은 결국 집을 짓고 가정을 꾸리는데 자신은 '그런 지혜를 경멸했다'며 가정의 기쁨도 거부했다고 담담히 인정하므로 D가 정답이다. A의 자부심, B의 원망, C의 혼란은 지문의 자기 성찰적 어조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: The police station lodging-house, where the soft side of a plank is the regulation couch, is next in order. The manner in which this police bed is "made up" is interesting in its simplicity. The loose planks that make the platform are simply turned over, and the job is done, with an occasional coat of white-wash thrown in to sweeten things. I know of only one easier way, but, so far as I am informed, it has never been introduced in this country. It used to be practised, if report spoke truly, in certain old-country towns.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: He views the police bed with dry mockery of its crude simplicity.
He sincerely admires the efficiency of the police bed's design.
He expresses open outrage and demands that the stations be reformed.
He feels nostalgic fondness for customs from old-country towns.
items.explanation: 화자는 판자의 '부드러운 면'이 규정 침대라고 비꼬고, 판자를 뒤집기만 하면 잠자리 정리가 끝난다며 '단순함이 흥미롭다'고 말한다. 석회 칠로 '향기롭게' 한다는 표현도 반어적이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 반어를 문자 그대로 읽은 것이고, C의 분노와 D의 향수는 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
The night was cloudy and black, and every line in the architecture of the largest building in the world was defined in light, even to the cross, which, as I have said before, is at the height of a mountain from the base. For about an hour it was a delicate but vast structure of shining lines, like a drawing of a glorious temple on the clouds. At eight, as the clock struck, flakes of fire burst from every point, and the whole building seemed started into flame. It was done by a simultaneous kindling of torches in a thousand points, a man stationed at each. The glare seemed to exceed that of noonday. No description can give an idea of it.

I am not sure that I have not been a little tedious in describing the ceremonies of the holy week.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: He finds the illumination tiresome and wishes it had ended sooner.
He is awed by the spectacle yet worries he has described too much.
He doubts the religious meaning behind the week's ceremonies.
He is frightened by the sudden fire and fears for the building.
items.explanation: 화자는 성당의 윤곽이 빛으로 그려진 모습을 '구름 위 영광스러운 신전'에 비유하며 '어떤 묘사로도 전할 수 없다'고 감탄한다. 그러면서 마지막에 성주간 의식을 너무 지루하게 묘사한 것은 아닌지 걱정하므로 B가 정답이다. A의 지루함, C의 의심, D의 공포는 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Not that it must be for a moment supposed that our Women are destitute of affection. But unfortunately the passion of the moment predominates, in the Frail Sex, over every other consideration. This is, of course, a necessity arising from their unfortunate conformation. For as they have no pretensions to an angle, being inferior in this respect to the very lowest of the Isosceles, they are consequently wholly devoid of brain-power, and have neither reflection, judgment nor forethought, and hardly any memory. Hence, in their fits of fury, they remember no claims and recognize no distinctions.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: It argues that women are more affectionate by nature than men are.
It describes one woman's violent outburst and its consequences.
It gives the narrator's explanation of why women act on sudden passion.
It questions the reasoning ability of the lowest Isosceles figures.
items.explanation: 서술자는 여성이 애정이 없는 것은 아니지만 순간의 감정이 다른 모든 고려를 압도한다고 말한다. 그 이유를 각이 없는 몸의 구조 때문에 판단력과 기억력이 없다는 데서 찾으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 비교 주장이 없고, B의 특정 사건과 D의 이등변삼각형 비판은 지문의 요지가 아니다.

items.passage:
In the end she rejected both courses and decided for the riding costume. The reason she gave for this decision--the reason she gave herself--was that the riding costume would invest the call with an air of accident, of impulse. The real reason.

It may be that some feminine reader can guess why she chose the most startling, the most gracefully becoming, the most artlessly physical apparel in her wardrobe.

She said nothing to her father at lunch about her plans. Why should she speak of them? He might oppose; also, she might change her mind. After lunch she set out on her usual ride, galloping away into the hills--but she had put twenty-five dollars in bills in her trousers pocket.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: It shows a woman openly arguing with her father about her plans.
It shows the narrator criticizing the woman's choice of clothing.
It describes an ordinary ride taken purely for exercise in the hills.
It reveals a woman's concealed motives and quiet preparations for a call.
items.explanation: 그녀는 승마복을 고르며 '우연한 방문처럼 보이려고'라는 이유를 스스로에게 대지만, 서술자는 '진짜 이유'가 따로 있음을 암시한다. 또 아버지에게 계획을 말하지 않고 평소처럼 말을 타러 나가면서 몰래 돈을 챙기므로 D가 정답이다. A는 아버지와 말다툼하지 않았고, B와 C는 지문의 의도를 놓친다.

items.passage:
Every hand was hard at work over its appointed task, and there was no evidence in that silent well-ordered hive, of the recent little revolution.

When the mathematician, having made his way to his own work-bench, had passed his unerring hand over it, he found all as he had left it—not a thing disturbed; every tool, every scrap of metal, every morsel of wire lying intact. Even the little steel coil which had come to such sudden grief, had been carefully rewound into proper compass, and placed ready to hand by Isaac Habrecht. “It is correctly adjusted, I think?” he said, as Dasipodius took it up.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: It shows the workshop restored to order, with even the damage quietly mended.
It depicts a revolt in the workshop that is still spreading among workers.
It describes the mathematician's anger on discovering his tools missing.
It reveals that Isaac Habrecht damaged the steel coil on purpose.
items.explanation: 지문은 조용한 작업장에 최근의 작은 '혁명'의 흔적이 전혀 없다고 말한다. 수학자가 작업대를 살펴보니 모든 것이 그대로였고, 망가졌던 코일까지 다시 감겨 준비되어 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 이미 끝난 소동을 진행 중이라 보고, C와 D는 지문 내용과 반대된다.
